Bacterial spot: Bacterial spot (Xanthomonas). Remove affected leaves, avoid overhead watering, and use copper-based sprays as a preventive. Rotate crops next season.
Early blight: Early blight (Alternaria). Remove lower infected leaves, mulch to stop soil splash, and space plants for airflow. Fungicides with chlorothalonil or copper help.
Late blight: Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) spreads fast in cool, wet weather. Remove and bag infected plants and tell nearby growers. Preventive fungicides are the main control.
Leaf Mold: Leaf mold (Passalora fulva) thrives in humid greenhouses. Increase ventilation, reduce humidity, and remove affected leaves.
Septoria leaf spot: Septoria leaf spot. Remove infected lower leaves, avoid wetting foliage, and apply a protective fungicide. Rotate crops.
Spider mites: Two-spotted spider mites. Spray leaf undersides with water or insecticidal soap; encourage predatory mites. Mites thrive in hot, dry conditions.
Target Spot: Target spot (Corynespora). Improve airflow, remove debris, and use a labelled fungicide if it spreads.
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus: Yellow leaf curl virus is spread by whiteflies. There's no cure: remove infected plants, control whiteflies, and use resistant varieties.
Tomato mosaic virus: Tomato mosaic virus spreads on hands and tools. Remove infected plants, disinfect tools, wash hands, and choose resistant varieties.
